taxonomic_note: The B088 source row uses 'Oenothera xerogaura', an outdated/malformed Drummond's-beeblossom concept. Current Kew accepts Oenothera hispida; Oenothera xenogaura and Gaura drummondii are synonyms.
look_here_first: Look for an aggressively rhizomatous, hairy perennial with small white-to-pink gaura flowers and mature fruits conspicuously swollen or bulging on the upper half.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis — type locality Austin, Travis County. Comal — historical type material of Gaura roemeriana from New Braunfels. Mason — Mason Mountain WMA flora documents Gaura drummondii.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Old Gaura drummondii and Oenothera xenogaura records map to the current accepted Oenothera hispida.

best_field_traits: fruit with conspicuously swollen upper portion
mature fruit is critical for separation from O. suffrutescens
morphology_keys.comparison_training: O. hispida can resemble O. suffrutescens strongly. Use mature capsules: O. hispida has distinctly expanded upper fruit lobes, whereas O. suffrutescens has a thick stipe and less abruptly swollen fruit.
